title: Isa's answer
hookLine: on the Day, Isa answers that he only said what he was told: worship Allah, my Lord and yours (5:116–118)

cards: A rumor grows in the retelling. A text gets screenshotted without the message before it. Someone is quoted saying what they never said, and wants one thing: to stand up and say, that's not what I said.

Here's what I said, word for word. Surah five ends with a scene set not in the past but on the Day of Judgment. Allah addresses Isa, son of Maryam, directly, in front of everyone, and asks him what he told people.
And Isa gives his answer, on the record.

teach.b: Verse one-sixteen. Allah asks: O Isa, son of Maryam, did you tell people to take you and your mother as two gods besides Allah? Isa's answer comes in layers.
First, glory to You. Then: it was not for me to say what I had no right to say. If I had said it, You would know it.
You know what is in my self, and I don't know what is in Yours.
Then verse one-seventeen, in Pickthall's words: “I spake unto them only that which Thou commandedst me, (saying): Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord.”
And: I was a witness over them while I lived among them, and after You took me, You were the watcher over them.

teach.h: ONLY THAT WHICH THOU COMMANDEDST ME.
teach.b: Then the last line, one-eighteen, which stands out for what it doesn't do. Isa doesn't ask for anyone to be punished.
He says: if You punish them, they are Your servants, and if You forgive them, You are the Mighty, the Wise. He leaves the outcome with God.

A report in the Sunan collections says the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ once spent a whole night in prayer repeating that single verse until dawn. Sahih Muslim records him reciting it and weeping for his own community.
Christians describe God as one God in three persons, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, and do not count Mary as part of God; Muslim commentators have discussed whom the question in this verse addresses.
The Qur'an's focus here is Isa himself: a prophet who said only what he was given, and then handed the rest back.

how: Muslims read 5:116–118 as Isa's testimony on the Day of Judgment, and some recite 5:118 in night prayer, following reports that the Prophet repeated it until dawn.

games.q: you're asked, in front of everyone, whether you said something you never said. what does Isa do first?
o: glorifies Allah, then says it wasn't his to say.
games.why: he begins with glory to You, then: it was not mine to say what I had no right to, and You know what is in my self.

practice: Think of something you've been passing along lately: a story about a coworker, a claim about the news. Ask gently: do I actually know this, or did I only hear about it?
If you're not sure, picture yourself saying, I don't know, or, that's all I was told, and let that feel light, not weak.

wordCard.voice: Isa's answer. On the Day, Isa says he told people only what he was commanded: worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: Isa, the Qur'an's name for Jesus, son of Maryam.

carryVoice: Your line: only what I was told. And with that, surah five, the Table Spread, is done.
